messages:
incident-bot: Pager: high error rate observed on /v1/generate in us-east-1 (>=15% 5m). Auto-escalating to on-call.
maya: on it, seeing spike in 500s from runtime-service-canary during rolling deploy.
devon: are these new model loads or just inference errors?
maya: looks like model-load failures (failed to decrypt model key) then downstream 500s. Logs: `ERROR KMS: AccessDenied`
akshay: omg, we just rotated the model encryption key in the KMS earlier in this deploy job — did the service principal get updated?
ops-sre: paging @akshay and @devon, which service account should have kms:Decrypt for the new key?
akshay: deploy-sa should have access, policy change went through but i think the key alias was renamed. The deploy manifest references `alias/redwood-models-v2` — ops said they'd rotate to `alias/redwood-models-v2-rotated` at 08:00.
devon: so the runtime is trying to decrypt with the old alias -> KMS returns AccessDenied when alias doesn't match key policy? weird — should be alias resolution.
maya: stack trace: `kmsclient: AccessDeniedException: User: arn:aws:sts::123:assumed-role/deploy-sa is not authorized to perform: kms:Decrypt on resource arn:aws:kms:us-east-1:123:key/abcd-rotated`
ellie: immediate mitigation: we should kill the canary rollout and flip the feature flag to force traffic back to stable. product-ops, can you toggle feature flag?
product-ops: doing it now — flipping `use-new-models-canary` -> false.
deploy-bot: Canary abort requested by product-ops. Rolling back canary to stable 2 instances.
maya: traffic is moving back now. Error rate dropping to baseline.
ops-sre: good. Next step: either re-grant deploy-sa the Decrypt permission on the new key or change the alias back. Which is safer?
akshay: safer to grant permission to deploy-sa on the new key with a tight condition for the alias. I'll open a short-lived policy change.
devon: do we have a secret fallback? a previously cached unencrypted key?
maya: runtime supports prefetched decrypted keys in KV cache, but new nodes didn't have it. So only old nodes still serving succeeded. That's why canary crashed.
ellie: customer impact assessment: this affected ~12% of requests in us-east-1 for ~6 minutes before rollback. No data exfiltration risk — failures were 5xx. We should mark incident customer-impact: partial outage for inference in us-east-1 during deploy.
product-ops: drafting a brief to customers: short blip during deploy, rollback performed, no persisted data affected.
ops-sre: policy change applied: `aws:kms:decrypt` allowed for deploy-sa on key `abcd-rotated` with request-time condition. Verifying...
akshay: policy looks good. I'll kick a canary redeploy but first will test a single instance with updated env var `KMS_KEY_ALIAS=alias/redwood-models-v2-rotated`.
devon: also updating the deploy job to resolve alias to key-id before rolling to runtime, to avoid alias race. Add a small wait after key rotation.
maya: re-deploying single canary instance now.
deploy-bot: new canary instance started (instance-id i-0abc).
maya: canary model loaded successfully. No KMS errors in logs.
ops-sre: monitoring for 10m before we promote. Errors flat.
ellie: timeline for postmortem: quick blameless write-up, root cause: key alias rotation without granting decrypt to deploy SA, contributing factor: immediate canary rollout post-rotation.
akshay: action items: 1) add pre-deploy KMS key validation step 2) update key rotation runbook 3) enforce IAM checks in CI 4) add alert for KMS AccessDenied spikes.
product-ops: customer comms sent to affected tenants at 12:24 UTC.
maya: handing back to on-call rotation — ops-sre will follow up. Thanks everyone. :heart:
ops-sre: will own the postmortem and follow through on the action items. Closing thread when postmortem link exists.
